PullRequest.Title: chat: show model provider logos on subagents and routing rows
PullRequest.Body:

Chat names the model at work in several places, and a name alone is slow to scan when a turn spreads across providers. This puts the logo of the model's provider beside each of those names, behind a new experimental setting.

## What changes

Everything here is behind `chat.modelLogos.enabled`, which is tagged Experimental and is on by default except in Stable. With the setting off, the chat renders as before.

- **Subagent and Copilot Fusion pass pills** show the provider's logo before the model name.
- **Routing rows** lead with the logo. It is the shared row, so this covers Auto, Copilot Fusion and model routers. The logo and the row's text sit in the same columns as the tool rows' icons and text.
- **Copilot Fusion at High and Max effort** named no model for the pass that writes into the chat. The agent host now names that model on its Fusion milestones, and the chat shows it in the same "Copilot Fusion routed task to …" row as Standard effort, once per change of model.
- **The notice of a routing that failed** reads with the fallback model's display name, led by its logo, in place of the model id.

Claude, Gemini and Microsoft show colored artwork. Other providers show their codicon in the icon color, and a provider without a logo shows none. High contrast themes show the single-color glyph for every provider. The logo is decorative and hidden from assistive technology, because the name beside it already says which model it is.

## Notes for reviewers

- The new High and Max rows are behind the same setting as the logos, so Stable does not change. They are hidden wherever the existing routing row is hidden.
- The pass's model travels as a new `vscode.chat.fusionPassModel` key in the `_meta` of the existing Fusion milestones. A host that does not send it gets no new row, and a client that ignores it is unaffected. A client that prints milestones as text sees one more line, such as "Follow-up pass started", when a pass's model changes.
- Three SVG files with the colored artwork are added under `chatContentParts/media/`. The Gemini one is an approximation of the spark.
- System notices with an icon, such as the routing-failed notice, start their text about 3px left of the tool rows' text. That is how they render on `main`, and this change leaves it alone.
- Four fixtures are new, so their screenshot baselines need accepting: `chat/chatAutoModeResolutionContentPart/ModelLogos`, `chat/chatRendering/ModelRoutingAmongTools`, `chat/chatSubagentContent/FusionCascadeModelLogos` and `chat/chatSubagentContent/ProviderModels`.

## How to test

1. Run a build that is not Stable, or turn on `chat.modelLogos.enabled`.
2. Start subagents on models from different providers. Each pill shows its provider's logo before the model name.
3. Send a turn with Auto or Copilot Fusion. The routing row leads with the routed model's logo, in line with the tool rows around it. At High or Max effort, the row names the model of the main pass.
4. Turn the setting off. The logos and the High and Max rows go away.

## Validation

All run on this branch after rebasing onto `main`.

- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <the 34 changed files>`: no findings.
- `pnpm run stylelint` on the two changed stylesheets: no findings.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `pnpm exec component-explorer render -p ./test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex 'chatRendering|chatAutoModeResolutionContentPart|chatSubagentContent'`: 162 fixtures rendered without errors.
- The unit tests below: 6786 passing, 3 pending.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Traced ChatDelta through updateResponsePart's new responseParts array, ChatStateSubscription's synchronous onDidChange, observableFromSubscription, and the new derived/autorun. DerivedImpl computes the value before applying equalsFn. fusionPassModels explicitly visits every part and allocates metadata objects for system notifications. Exact CPU time and frequency of very long turns are not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Response-part traversal and newly allocated system-notification metadata/row objects on the workbench thread.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For D relevant state/stream updates, adds O(sum(P_current)) active-part visits plus O(D * P_previous) predecessor-part visits, even when there are zero new Fusion model changes. Metadata allocations scale with the notifications revisited; effective emitted rows remain bounded by actual model changes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous workbench CPU and short-lived allocation during streaming, reducing responsiveness and delaying response updates as turns grow.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing reducer and keyed progress adapter handled streamed updates, but there was no Fusion-routing scan of the active transcript or repeated parsing of the completed predecessor transcript for each update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every streamed markdown/reasoning or tool update now rescans the active turn's responseParts for Fusion metadata, and every merged-state update rescans the completed predecessor's responseParts. Deduplicating the resulting rows does not deduplicate these computations, and disabled logos or non-Fusion turns still pay the scans once the explainability treatment is known.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added agentHostSessionHandler.ts:4559 derives fusionPassModels from the entire responseParts$ on every invalidation; added :4386 derives previousFusionPassModel directly from mergedState$. The new autorun reads this derived before the ModelLogos setting is checked, which only happens in toFusionPassResolution at :8212. Previously neither Fusion-specific scan existed.
Findings.Title: Avoid rescanning Fusion routing on every streamed update
Findings.Impact: Long, tool-heavy agent-host tasks followed by another streamed response repeatedly traverse hundreds of already-processed parts and reparse their notifications on the workbench thread, adding CPU/GC pressure and delaying progress rendering and input responsiveness. This also affects ordinary non-Fusion chats and Stable with model logos disabled.
Findings.Evidence: protocol/channels-chat/reducer.ts:371-376 and :294-325 replace the responseParts array for each ChatDelta; tool updates do likewise at :267-285. agentSubscription.ts:624-640 fires onDidChange per envelope, and :1514-1519 adapts it without debounce. The new derived at agentHostSessionHandler.ts:4559 invokes stateToProgressAdapter.ts:1067-1089's full loop; :1093-1097 repeats that loop for the previous completed turn on merged-state changes. readAgentSystemNotificationMeta constructs an object for every notification visited. observableInternal/observables/derivedImpl.ts:201-217 applies equality only after computing the value.
Findings.Recommendation: Consume Fusion model changes incrementally through the existing keyed notification handling, seed once when joining, and rebuild for snapshot replacement/truncation. Derive/cache the predecessor result from its responseParts identity rather than the whole merged state, and avoid activating this work when the feature is disabled.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream a long agent-host turn, including ordinary non-Fusion models, Fusion workflows, and model logos disabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each incoming chat action updates the subscription and synchronously evaluates workbench observables before progress delivery/rendering can finish. New Fusion scans execute on this path after the explainability treatment becomes known, even when logos are disabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive and parse action envelopes from the existing agent-host transport, then synchronously apply them to subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing streamed actions remain one per delivered envelope. Fusion additionally emits a small notification only when an inline pass changes model; the scans do not issue RPCs per response part.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same incoming stream and transport, without either Fusion-specific transcript scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Envelope processing reaches the new full scans before its observable update finishes on the workbench thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Add a model-id string to existing Fusion milestones and emit an additional pass-model notification for changed inline models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added string per applicable milestone and at most one added notification per accepted change of inline model, not per token or tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing milestones lacked this string and changed inline models did not generate the extra notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous construction/publication; does not initiate or await a new model invocation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D delivered deltas/tool/state updates, P_current parts in the active turn, P_previous parts in its completed predecessor, and N notifications among those parts. Long tool-heavy tasks can accumulate hundreds of parts and many streamed updates; emitted Fusion rows are only actual model changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous workbench-thread evaluation per delivered state change; no time-based debounce or in-flight coalescing for the new scans. Existing transport flow-control windows do not cache these computations. Subagent-only observers skip the added per-turn adjunct.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: derivedOpts equality suppresses unchanged output notifications only after full computation. The active responseParts array changes on each text/tool update. previousFusionPass$ depends on mergedState rather than the unchanged predecessor array. Neither scan caches parsed notifications; disabled/non-Fusion paths can repeatedly produce empty rows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reducer array replacement, synchronous subscription events, derived dependencies, full loops, metadata allocation, and post-computation equality are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or profiles available; prevalence of very large turns and exact CPU/GC time are uncertain. These affect severity, not the proven per-update multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity repeated-work regression: unconditional active and predecessor transcript scans during streaming. Model-change notification fan-out itself is bounded and not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen or reconnect a Copilot/Fusion chat and reconstruct completed history plus an active turn.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing session subscription hydration precedes chat hydration; cold SDK history pages and database enrichment complete before reconstructed turns can be shown. The added Fusion extraction then runs synchronously during history adaptation and active-turn seeding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to session and chat state and receive history snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing cold subscription per held resource, shared on warm access; reconnect refreshes existing channels. No added subscriptions for logos or Fusion model rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subscription count, hydration ordering, snapshots, and paging policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing hydration must complete before history/progress is adapted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the SDK event log via rpc.eventLog.read using cursor pages with max=1000 and includeEphemeral=false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized RPC per existing history page on a cold primary/all scope, with warm and concurrent callers coalesced by _mappedEventsMemo.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical event-log calls, scope, page size, filtering, and memoization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold event retrieval precedes mapping and display; no new process is spawned by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read recorded assistant responses/import metadata/completion references and batch-enrich file edits, tool resources, and retained shell-output sizes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed metadata reads plus one grouped file-edit read when edit calls exist, one grouped resource read when completions exist, and one grouped terminal-size read for all shell candidates across chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same database reads and grouping; no new per-model database calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold reconstruction awaits existing enrichment. Added Fusion parts do not qualify as edit/resource/shell candidates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain reconstructed pass-model milestones and create routing rows in the existing history representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by accepted model changes per workflow/turn; two added linear part scans per adapted turn. Payload growth is short model metadata/rows rather than copied child transcripts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No pass-model rows; existing reconstruction already traversed events and response parts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds synchronous mapping work before display, but no newly awaited I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E persisted SDK events (1000 maximum per requested page), T loaded turns, sum(P_turn) response parts, and K model changes. Relay chat history can be paged; local replay reads complete history within its scope.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session/chat hydration is awaited in its existing order. SDK history pages are cursor-serialized. _mappedEventsMemo coalesces callers per primary/all scope; database enrichment is batched. Replay loops are synchronous and buffered updates drain into their owning turn.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold reconstruction is memoized separately for primary and all-agent scope; warm callers reuse the same promise/result. Rejections are evicted for retry. Fusion replay resets its per-turn state and drains buffered updates. Workbench history adaptation adds two linear scans per turn, not one RPC per model or part.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged boundary counts, per-scope memoization, sequential pages, grouped database access, and linear added replay work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Total history size and cold retrieval latency vary; no benchmark measurements. New cold adaptation remains linear with bounded row output.
Scenarios.Verdict: No distinct high-confidence performance regression in cold history replay. Reconnected active streaming is covered by the reported repeated-scan issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render subagent/Fusion pills, Auto/router routing rows, and degraded routing notices with provider logos.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible content-part construction performs model identity lookup and a small DOM insertion. A degraded notice walks its already-rendered, short fallback sentence to locate the model name. No SDK/provider request is awaited for logo resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the packaged Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft SVG backgrounds for matching visible logos.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three distinct small assets on cold rendering, shared by all matching rows; warm resources reuse browser caching. No per-pill remote provider request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These colored artwork resources were not loaded by the content parts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Artwork paints after resource availability; text/name rendering does not await these files.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V mounted rows/pills, K actual routing model changes, and up to three distinct colored provider asset URLs. Providerless models show no logo; high-contrast themes use glyphs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous rendering per mounted content part. Metadata is read from an in-memory model map. No eager child-chat initialization or process/network fan-out was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: lookupLanguageModel is a Map.get, including absent-model results without remote lookup. Pill logo updates compare icon ids to avoid unchanged DOM writes. Browser resource caching shares each SVG URL across rows. Setting/model signals are shared, not separate service listeners per pill.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lookup implementation, identity guards, asset rules, and notification text source are traced. No changed forced geometry reads or live visual filters found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mounted row count and browser paint timings are not measured. SVGs are small and static; added nodes are bounded per mounted row.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering regression: bounded DOM/artwork additions implement the feature, and richer notification metadata does not create heavyweight renderer work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle model logos or change registered models while chat rows/pills are mounted, then close/dispose the chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/model events synchronously update mounted logo elements and relevant tooltip/configuration text. Disposal tears down content-part autoruns; notice-logo disposal restores text.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: V mounted observers, one model-logo configuration listener and the existing shared model-change signal; no retained per-history keys introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared observable configuration source per IConfigurationService, with per-mounted-part autoruns. Events fan out only to current observers; no subprocess or remote metadata requests are issued.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WeakMap keys configuration-service lifetime; observableFromEvent owns its listener while observed. Existing listener-count test was updated from one configuration listener to two settings and still expects zero after pill disposal. System-notice logo insertion uses reader.store cleanup on toggles/disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for shared listeners, weak ownership, registered disposal, and guarded DOM updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large numbers of simultaneously mounted pills could increase toggle cost; toggles/model registration are not token-frequency events. No measured timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence retention, cleanup, or configuration fan-out regression. No transitive external boundary is invoked by the changed logo-update helpers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over all 34 changed files and every diff page (all nextOffset values zero). Traced rendering/lifecycle, live streaming, cold/warm reconstruction, subscription transport, SDK history RPCs, and grouped database enrichment. Submitted one introduced repeated-work finding anchored to the new streaming derived. No concrete removed performance regression qualified for blame/fix reporting. Static read-only review; measured magnitude remains unknown.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
